title: Mysore Pak
instructions: Roast the besan lightly in a pan on low heat, making sure it does not change color.
In another pan, boil the sugar and water until the syrup becomes slightly sticky (about one-string consistency).
Slowly add the roasted besan to the syrup, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Add the warm ghee little by little and keep stirring until the mixture becomes thick and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Pour it into a greased plate and spread evenly.
Let it cool slightly, then cut into small squares or diamonds. Allow it to cool completely before serving.
story: This Mysore Pak is very special to me because it is my mom's favorite sweet. When she makes it, we both love to eat it together and spend time with each other. When my mom was young, her parents were farmers. They had cows at home, so they made their own ghee, and they had a lot of jaggery (cane sugar). My grandma used to make this sweet because it was easy to make and enough for all the children. So, this sweet has a lot of family memories for my mom, and now it is special to me too.
